items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: That's when I substituted for Madison Reed for Eubie Blake, when Eubie Blake had me come up there. He was sick in Baltimore.

ctx.x: When did you first hear -- had you heard blues at this point in Philadelphia?

Oh, yes. Oh, yeah, you heard that with the guitars. The guy would stand on the corner and they'd be selling oysters or something like that. Or there'd be a blind man playing that, you know, we'd filled a pepper pot. And most of the guys were like from Baltimore. That was Eubie Blake's home, Baltimore. And Chick Webb's home was Baltimore. A lot of the musicians and all. But Baltimore was a great center for music, too.. Philadelphia was. Philadelphia piano players. Baltimore give you guitars, and tenor banjoes and…

Then, as you go farther south, the poor people were poorer, and they didn't even have those instruments. I've seen guys make as much music as Gene Krupa or Chick Webb with two bones. They'd just take these two bones and rattle them, clack, clack, clack, and could really to do a dance. So, as far as that goes, they been havin' to do that because we didn't have anything else.
